title: Platform-Specific Implementations
subtopics: Avoiding Platform Dependencies in Common Code
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of platform-specific implementations using at least one correct term from the lesson.

Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Platform-Specific Implementations** as part of **Kotlin Multiplatform and Compose Multiplatform**. Kotlin Multiplatform organizes shared logic and target-specific implementations through source sets; only APIs available for every configured target belong in common code. Use the subtopics—expect and actual Declarations, Common Interfaces and Platform Implementations, Avoiding Platform Dependencies in Common Code—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Multiplatform work succeeds when shared code depends only on common APIs and platform-specific code is isolated behind deliberate interfaces.

items.title: Common Interfaces and Platform Implementations
items.text: Common Interfaces and Platform Implementations should support a clear object invariant: make valid states easy to represent, restrict mutation to the intended API, and keep initialization and dependencies explicit.

content_blocks.code:
data class Greeting(val text: String)

fun greetingFor(name: String): Greeting = Greeting("Hello, $name")

fun main() = println(greetingFor("Kotlin").text)
content_blocks.run_instructions: Run inside a Kotlin Multiplatform project with the target toolchains installed; common and platform-specific source sets have different APIs.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the documented starting values, rerun the smallest test, and compare the result with the expected output. If behavior differs, check the compiler/plugin/runtime versions and the active target before changing more than one thing.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: Platform-Specific Implementations removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.
